'''Chiasmus''' is a secret German government [[block cipher]] that was leaked by [[reverse engineering]]. It became notorious for its dilettante use in the [[Federal Office for Information Security|BSI]]'s software {{ill|GSTOOL|de}}, which used it in insecure [[Block cipher mode of operation#ECB|Electronic Codebook (ECB)]] mode and generated the key with a [[Pseudorandom number generator|pseudo random number generator]] initialized to the current system time, which means an effective key length that can easily be broken by [[Brute-force attack|brute force]]. The [[BSI Group|BSI]] tried to prevent the publication of these findings with legal threats.

Chiasmus seems to be resistant against the most common cryptographic attacks ([[Linear cryptanalysis|linear]] and [[differential cryptanalysis]]), but a lot slower than the openly available state of the art ciphers such as [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Chiasmus for Windows |url=https://www.ia.nato.int/niapc/Product/Chiasmus-for-Windows_312 |website=www.ia.nato.int |access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Chiasmus (cipher) |url=https://memim.com/chiasmus-cipher.html |website=memim.com |access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref>
